title: F1: cribl-decision names the technique family without retrieval (one head over every ATT&CK family)
question: Can the model, reading only the sentence, name the ATT&CK technique family better than the retrieve-then-pick arms (B1, B3), whose answer is capped by whether the pipeline's top 10 contain the family (CTI-HAL 0.852, public test 0.878, clean AnnoCTR test about 0.87)?

model.base: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base @ 1001bb4d, 4-bit NF4, bf16 compute, as B1-B3
model.prompt: chat format; the C1 state (sentence + source note) and a family question; no options; the decision slot is the last position (after 'Answer:')
model.head: scaled cosine (initial scale 16, learnable) between the centred decision-slot state and one row per family, plus a bias; 222 families = the active parent techniques of the C1 catalogue (ATT&CK 19.2); each row starts as the mean decision-slot state of the family's own texts (parent and sub-techniques, label + cut description, read by the starting adapter); the centre is the mean of the rows
model.readout: softmax over all 222 families; the pick is the most probable family (never abstains)

data.train: cases_train.jsonl (public train splits, 6,308 rows, deduplicated against dev/test/CTI-HAL as before) + cases_annoctr_train.jsonl (clean AnnoCTR train, 1,453 rows); target = the case's gold families (uniform), every row used whether or not retrieval found it; rows whose gold has no catalogue family are skipped and counted
data.annoctr_rebuild: AnnoCTR was rebuilt before this registration: prepare_annoctr.py now joins _context_left + mention + _context_right (the stripped context_* fields glued the mention to its neighbours, e.g. 'installsransomware') and strips markdown links with a title and images; one sentence with several mention spans is now one case (train 1,500, dev 336, test 738 scorable). B3's inputs are kept in data/audits/cribl_ft/b3_inputs/
data.dev: cases_dev.jsonl (public dev, 659) and cases_annoctr_dev.jsonl (clean AnnoCTR dev, 336)
data.confirmation: CTI-HAL statements (968; local only, never leaves this machine), public test (1,391), clean AnnoCTR test (738)

fixed.training: LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3, AdamW without weight decay, cosine schedule with 3% warmup, 16 examples per optimizer step (batch 1), 3 epochs, gradient clipping 1.0, max 1,024 prompt tokens, seed 7
fixed.checkpoints: step_0 (the untrained head: nearest family description, reported as F0) and every half epoch
fixed.compute: the local RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (8 GB), about 3.5 h; no OpenRouter credit, no pods

selection.checkpoint: the highest mean of family top-1 over public dev and clean AnnoCTR dev; ties the earlier

references: on the same rows: pipeline rank-1 family; B1 step_9462 and B3 step_7088 retrieve-then-pick under never-abstain (their stored CTI-HAL and public test predictions; both scored once on clean AnnoCTR test after F1's checkpoint is selected); Jev C1 as reported and under never-abstain on CTI-HAL

success.headline: CTI-HAL family top-1: F1 minus B3 (never-abstain), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: CTI-HAL family top-1: F1 minus pipeline rank-1, paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
clean AnnoCTR test family top-1: F1 minus B3, paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
public test family top-1: F1 minus B1, paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
CTI-HAL: F1's top-5 contains the gold family at least as often as the pipeline's top 10 (0.852), the condition for using F1 as the candidate generator in a follow-up

stop_rules: a checkpoint does not reload (adapter check)
the training loss is not finite
more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and clean AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
reporting: every checkpoint's dev curve, F0 and F1 family top-1/3/5, MRR and ECE on every set and per dataset, explicit vs implicit AnnoCTR mentions, the paired deltas above, training time
informed_by: the B1/B2/B3 dev and confirmation results (docs 21.3.18); B1 and B3 on clean AnnoCTR dev (family 0.527 / 0.693, pipeline 0.470); a pilot of 160 train rows scored on the first 40 cases of each dev set (mechanics and speed only: step_0 top-1 0.40 public dev, 0.25 AnnoCTR dev); a batching check (no speed gain, so batch 1). No F model has been scored on a confirmation set.
follow_up_not_registered: the same recipe on Qwen3.5-9B-Base (RunPod) to measure model size; a sub-technique step inside the predicted family; F1 as candidate generator for the C1 picker

amendments.before: any F1 training step: the local start was stopped by the owner while it scored the untrained head (step_0) on public dev; those partial step_0 predictions were deleted unread
amendments.change: training, dev selection and the public test / clean AnnoCTR test confirmations run on a RunPod secure RTX 4090 ($0.89/h) with scripts/cribl_finetune/runpod/remote_f1.sh; the B1/B3 references on clean AnnoCTR test are scored on the pod too; CTI-HAL is not uploaded: the selected checkpoint is downloaded and scored on CTI-HAL on the laptop
amendments.reason: the owner asked for RunPod instead of the 3.5 h laptop run
amendments.deviation: GPU floating-point differences against the laptop; same code, data, seed and settings

amendments.before: any F1 training checkpoint: the pod run was stopped at optimizer step 10 of 1,456, after the untrained head's dev scores (step_0: public dev top-1 0.451, AnnoCTR dev 0.226)
amendments.change: 16 examples per forward pass (left-padded with an attention mask) instead of batch 1; still 16 examples per optimizer step and the per-example loss summed and divided by 16, so the update rule is unchanged; dev and confirmation scoring are batched the same way
amendments.reason: on the RTX 4090 pod batch 1 was CPU-bound (GPU 11-14% busy, one core at 100%, 0.95 s/example, about 6 h); the laptop batching check had shown no gain only because its GPU is the bottleneck
amendments.deviation: padding and batched kernels change floating-point results slightly (decision-slot states match batch 1 at cosine > 0.9997 in the check); the training data order is unchanged
amendments.informed_by: the untrained head's dev scores and the speed of the first 10 optimizer steps; nothing from a trained F1 checkpoint

amendments.before: any test or CTI-HAL scoring under this rule (the top-1 confirmation results were already read; the rule's test numbers were not computed)
amendments.change: a second decision rule, reported beside top-1: name the most probable family plus every other family of the top 3 whose probability is at least 0.25; scored as family micro precision/recall/F1 (scripts/cribl_finetune/multi_family.py); the threshold was chosen on public dev + AnnoCTR dev of the selected checkpoint only (grid 0.05-0.50 and top-1 only, mean F1, ties the higher threshold; data/audits/cribl_ft/F1_multi_family_tune.json): dev mean F1 0.670 -> 0.677
amendments.reason: the owner asked for a higher F1; 7% of CTI-HAL statements and 18% of public test cases have more than one gold family, which a single answer always misses
amendments.success: reported only: no criterion, the top-1 results above stay the registered outcome
amendments.informed_by: the top-1 confirmation results and the dev predictions; no test scores under the rule
